verses.1: Brothers, I could not speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to worldly people, as to infants in the Messiah.
verses.2: I fed you with milk, not solid food, for you were not yet able. And you are still not able,
verses.3: for you are still worldly. For where there is jealousy and strife among you, are you not worldly and acting as mere humans?
verses.4: For when one says, "I follow Paul," and another, "I follow Apollos," are you not mere humans?
verses.5: What is Apollos? What is Paul? Only servants through whom you believed, and as the Lord assigned to each, so one ministers.
verses.6: I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth;
verses.7: so that neither the one who plants is anything, nor the one who waters, but God who gives the growth.
verses.8: The one who plants and the one who waters are one, and each will receive their own reward according to their own labor,
verses.9: for we are God's co-workers; you are God's field, God's building.
verses.10: According to the grace given to me, I laid a foundation like a skillful master builder, and another is building upon it. Each one must carefully consider how they build,
verses.11: for no one can lay any other foundation than the one already laid, which is Jesus the Messiah;
verses.12: if anyone builds on this foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, straw,
verses.13: each person’s work will become evident, for the day will disclose it, because it is revealed by fire, and the fire itself will test the quality of each person’s work.
verses.14: If anyone’s work survives what they built, they will receive a reward;
verses.15: if anyone’s work is burned up, they will suffer loss, though they themselves will be saved—but only as through fire.
verses.16: Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?
verses.17: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy that person, for God’s temple is holy, and you are that temple.
verses.18: Do not deceive yourselves. If anyone among you considers themselves wise in this age, they must become a fool, so that they may become truly wise,
verses.19: for the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. It is written, “He catches the wise in their craftiness,”
verses.20: and again, “The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, how they are empty.”
verses.21: So no one should boast in people, for all things are yours,
verses.22: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or present things or things to come—all are yours,
verses.23: and you are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "σαρκίνοις" and "νηπίοις" are rendered as "worldly people" and "infants" to preserve the contrast with spiritual maturity.
- v. 2: "γάλα" and "βρῶμα" are rendered as "milk" and "solid food" to reflect the metaphor of spiritual nourishment.
- v. 3: "σαρκικοί" is translated as "worldly" rather than "fleshly" to align with Paul's contrast between the spiritual and the worldly mindset.
- v. 6-7: "φυτεύσα" and "ποτίζων" are translated as "planted" and "watered" to maintain the agricultural metaphor.
- v. 11: "θεμέλιον" is translated as "foundation" to emphasize the unchangeable base of Christ.
- v. 12-15: The metaphor of materials being burned by fire is retained in full to reflect the evaluative imagery.
